rationale: This is essentially a re-normalization of the archived "Firm-Specific Funding and Investment Peaks" (deviation-from-own-3yr-MA in place of TS_RANK over the same investment and external-financing constructs), i.e., a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively new mechanism.

It is the archived "Deployed External Capital Bottleneck" with the cash-retention leg — the component that plausibly drove that signal's strength — removed and total external financing merely split into its equity and debt halves, so it is a weaker rediscovery of an already-evaluated construct (and of the well-known composite external-financing anomaly).

Internally consistent and a genuine funding-channel switch relative to the archived debt-funded hiring signal, though the equity-issuance level gate and the equity-minus-debt tilt are largely redundant with each other and the components (employee growth, net share issuance) are individually well-documented anomalies.

Introduces a genuinely new conditioning dimension (pre-existing balance-sheet capacity, correctly lagged to avoid mechanical contamination) rather than recombining the same investment-financing pair, and the expected negative sign is coherent with both the leverage puzzle and investment-overextension logic.

The simultaneous-issuance-and-distribution conjunction is a legitimately novel angle, but the payout leg is a well-established *positive* return predictor pulling against the stated negative sign, so the composite's expected direction is theoretically ambiguous and the gross-flow terms will tilt toward large mature firms.

"Stock-financed acquirers underperform" is a textbook published anomaly (Loughran-Vijh, Rau-Vermaelen) built from two individually known effects (goodwill/acquisition intensity and net share issuance), and it closely echoes the archived Debt-Funded Acquisition Footprint with the financing leg simply swapped.
